# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Apr 16, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on significant contract enhancements, including the addition of ZK dispute game roots and removal of OPCMv1 code, alongside critical bug fixes and documentation improvements.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### ZK Dispute Game Integration and Contract Refinements
The Optimism team integrated ZK dispute game roots into the contracts, enhancing the dispute resolution mechanisms. This involved adding new interfaces and implementations for `ZKDisputeGame`, `AccessManager`, and `ZKVerifier`, alongside updates to deployment scripts and ABI snapshots. Concurrently, all remaining OPCMv1 code was removed from `op-deployer`, `op-chain-ops`, and `op-core`, streamlining the codebase and removing deprecated features.
[#19685](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19685), [#20064](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20064)

### L2 Contracts Manager and EIP-7825 Enhancements
A critical fix was implemented for the L2 Contracts Manager to guard CGT feature activation and liquidity controller renounce ownership, improving contract security and upgradeability. Additionally, a new acceptance test was added to verify the EIP-7825 transaction gas limit cap, ensuring compliance with the Karst upgrade.
[#20095](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20095), [#20070](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20070)

### Documentation and Interoperability Improvements
Documentation received attention with fixes for typos and broken links across public-facing guides and tutorials. A governance proposal link was also added to the stake-based priority ordering notice and priority fee info box. In other work, unused interoperability contracts and their references were removed, simplifying the contract landscape.
[#20131](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20131), [#20127](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20127), [#19999](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19999)

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS

- [#20132](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20132) ci: stop running contracts tests in both main and contracts-feature-tests
- [#20130](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20130) feat: risczero adapter standalone
- [#20129](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20129) ci: retry apt-get update on transient mirror sync failures
- [#20128](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20128) U19 notice page draft
- [#20126](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20126) ci: bump factory workflow to node24-compatible version
- [#20123](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20123) op-acceptance-tests: add interop activation boundary fault proof test
- [#20121](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20121) chore(ci): add ci-base-clang image and register for factory builds
- [#20118](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20118) chore(ci): skip example crates on PR branches to speed up Rust builds
- [#20117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20117) chore(ops): add ci-base-clang image scripts
- [#20116](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20116) test(contracts): improve OptimismSuperchainERC20Beacon test coverage
- [#20115](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20115) refactor(op-alloy-consensus): deposit source hash builder

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Interoperability and Supervisor Enhancements
Several issues related to interoperability and the `op-supervisor` were closed, including those concerning slow sync times, address book fixes, and the removal of multi-node support. This indicates a push towards a more streamlined and efficient interop system.

Several issues tracking the Interop release, including end-to-end testing checklists, defining processes for adding new chains, and descope of liquidity migration contracts, have been closed. This indicates significant progress towards the Interop mainnet release.
